CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain for one week. Pain began during a gymnastics class when patient may have fallen or assumed an unusual position during an activity. She described going "overboard" with the move. Patient attempted self-treatment with Tylenol for 2-3 days without relief. She reports pain with any movement of the left shoulder.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prior surgery on left arm

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (acetaminophen) taken for 2-3 days without relief

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Participates in gymnastics class

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient reports pain with movement of left shoulder in forward and backward directions. States any kind of movement of left shoulder causes pain.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fracture or broken bone noted.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Assessment: Left shoulder joint injury

Plan:
1. Ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week
2. Ice or heat pad as needed for pain relief
3. Rest left arm during healing
4. Avoid carrying heavy weights
5. Use right hand for activities for 3-4 weeks
6. Follow-up appointment in 3 weeks
7. If pain persists after 3 weeks, may consider repeat x-ray
8. Patient may call office if pain worsens or to request earlier appointment
9. Alternative pain relievers: Advil or Aleve
